items.informal_name: Lower Bound for Polynomial Evaluation at Rational Points
items.type:
∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K] {f : Polynomial ℤ} {a b : ℤ},
  0 < b →
    Polynomial.eval (↑a / ↑b) (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℤ K) f) ≠ 0 →
      1 ≤ ↑b ^ f.natDegree * |Polynomial.eval (↑a / ↑b) (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℤ K) f)|
items.informal_description: For any linearly ordered field $ K $ with strict ordered ring structure, given a non-zero polynomial $ f \in \mathbb{Z}[X] $, integers $ a, b $ with $ b > 0 $, and assuming $ f\left(\frac{a}{b}\right) \neq 0 $, it holds that $ 1 \leq b^{\deg(f)} \cdot \left| f\left(\frac{a}{b}\right) \right| $, where $ \deg(f) $ denotes the natural degree of $ f $.

items.type: {K : Type u_1} → [inst : NormedDivisionRing K] → Polynomial K → NNReal
items.informal_description: The Cauchy bound of a polynomial $ p $ over a normed division ring $ K $ is defined as $ 1 + \frac{\sup_{0 \leq i < \deg p} \|\text{coeff}_i(p)\|}{\|\text{leadingCoeff}(p)\|} $, where $ \sup $ denotes the supremum of the absolute values of the coefficients excluding the leading term, and $ \|\cdot\| $ is the norm on $ K $. This provides an upper bound on the absolute values of the roots of $ p $.

items.informal_name: Liouville's Approximation Theorem for Irrational Roots of Integer Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {α : ℝ},
  Irrational α →
    ∀ {f : Polynomial ℤ},
      f ≠ 0 →
        Polynomial.eval α (Polynomial.map (algebraMap ℤ ℝ) f) = 0 →
          ∃ A, 0 < A ∧ ∀ (a : ℤ) (b : ℕ), 1 ≤ (↑b + 1) ^ f.natDegree * (|α - ↑a / (↑b + 1)| * A)
items.informal_description: Let $\alpha$ be an irrational real number and let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be a non-zero polynomial such that $f(\alpha) = 0$. Then there exists a positive real number $A$ such that for all integers $a$ and natural numbers $b$, the inequality $1 \leq A \cdot (b + 1)^{\deg(f)} \cdot |\alpha - \frac{a}{b + 1}|$ holds.

items.informal_name: Denominators Clearable Given Bounded Polynomial Degree
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring K] {i : R →+* K} {b : R} {bi : K} (N : ℕ)
  (a : R), bi * i b = 1 → ∀ (f : Polynomial R), f.natDegree ≤ N → DenomsClearable a b N f i
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ f $ with natural degree $ \leq N $, there exist elements $ D \in R $ and $ \beta \in K $ such that $ \beta \cdot i(b) = 1 $ and $ i(D) = i(b)^N \cdot \text{eval}_{i(a)\beta}(f^i) $, where $ f^i $ denotes the polynomial obtained by applying the ring homomorphism $ i $ to each coefficient of $ f $.

items.informal_name: Denominator Divides Leading Coefficient for Roots in Fraction Ring
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : IsDomain A] [inst_2 : UniqueFactorizationMonoid A]
  [inst_3 : Field K] [inst_4 : Algebra A K] [inst_5 : IsFractionRing A K] {p : Polynomial A} {r : K},
  (Polynomial.aeval r) p = 0 → ↑(IsFractionRing.den A r) ∣ p.leadingCoeff
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ A $ and an element $ r $ in the fraction ring $ K $ of $ A $, if $ r $ is a root of $ p $ (i.e., $ \text{aeval}(r, p) = 0 $), then the denominator $ \text{den}(r) $ of $ r $ (as defined in the fraction ring) divides the leading coefficient of $ p $. This generalizes the classical Rational Root Theorem to fraction rings of commutative semirings.

items.name: Polynomial.le_rootMultiplicity_map
items.type: {A : Type u_1} {B : Type u_2} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] {p : Polynomial A} {f : A →+* B} (hmap : Polynomial.map f p ≠ 0) (a : A) : Polynomial.rootMultiplicity a p ≤ Polynomial.rootMultiplicity (f a) (Polynomial.map f p)

items.type: {A : Type u_1} {B : Type u_2} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain A] [DecidableEq B] (p : Polynomial A) {f : A →+* B} (hf : Function.Injective ⇑f) (b : B) : Multiset.count b (Multiset.map (⇑f) p.roots) ≤ Polynomial.rootMultiplicity b (Polynomial.map f p)

items.informal_name: Denominator Divides Leading Coefficient for Roots in Fraction Ring
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : IsDomain A] [inst_2 : UniqueFactorizationMonoid A]
  [inst_3 : Field K] [inst_4 : Algebra A K] [inst_5 : IsFractionRing A K] {p : Polynomial A} {r : K},
  (Polynomial.aeval r) p = 0 → ↑(IsFractionRing.den A r) ∣ p.leadingCoeff
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ A $ and an element $ r $ in the fraction ring $ K $ of $ A $, if $ r $ is a root of $ p $ (i.e., $ \text{aeval}(r, p) = 0 $), then the denominator $ \text{den}(r) $ of $ r $ (as defined in the fraction ring) divides the leading coefficient of $ p $. This generalizes the classical Rational Root Theorem to fraction rings of commutative semirings.

items.informal_name: Divisibility by Normalized Coprime Polynomial Factor
items.type:
∀ {K : Type u} [inst : Field K] (p : Polynomial K) {q : Polynomial K},
  q ≠ 0 → Polynomial.C (q / gcd p q).leadingCoeff⁻¹ * (p / gcd p q) ∣ p
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ and non-zero polynomial $ q $ over a field $ K $, the product of the constant polynomial with coefficient equal to the inverse of the leading coefficient of $ q / \gcd(p, q) $ and the polynomial $ p / \gcd(p, q) $ divides $ p $. This constructs a normalized coprime divisor of $ p $ by adjusting the leading coefficient of the coprime part of $ q $.

items.informal_name: Numerator and Denominator are Relatively Prime in Fraction Ring
items.informal_description: For every element $ x $ in the fraction ring $ K $ of a commutative semiring $ A $, the numerator $ \text{num}(x) $ and denominator $ \text{den}(x) $ of its reduced fraction representation satisfy the property that they are relatively prime, meaning every common divisor of $ \text{num}(x) $ and $ \text{den}(x) $ is a unit in $ A $.

items.informal_name: Rational Root Theorem: Numerator Divides Constant Term
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : IsDomain A] [inst_2 : UniqueFactorizationMonoid A]
  [inst_3 : Field K] [inst_4 : Algebra A K] [inst_5 : IsFractionRing A K] {p : Polynomial A} {r : K},
  (Polynomial.aeval r) p = 0 → IsFractionRing.num A r ∣ p.coeff 0
items.informal_description: If $ r $ is a root of the polynomial $ p $ in the fraction ring $ K $ of a commutative semiring $ A $, then the numerator of $ r $ divides the constant term $ p(0) $ of $ p $.

items.informal_name: Numerator is Root of Scaled Polynomial when Element is Root
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : Field K] [inst_2 : Algebra A K]
  [inst_3 : IsFractionRing A K] [inst_4 : IsDomain A] [inst_5 : UniqueFactorizationMonoid A] {p : Polynomial A} {x : K},
  (Polynomial.aeval x) p = 0 → (p.scaleRoots ↑(IsFractionRing.den A x)).IsRoot (IsFractionRing.num A x)
items.informal_description: If $ x $ is a root of a polynomial $ p $ in the fraction ring $ K $ of a commutative semiring $ A $, then the numerator of $ x $ is a root of the polynomial obtained by scaling $ p $ by the denominator of $ x $. Formally, if $ \text{aeval}(x, p) = 0 $, then $ \text{num}(x) $ is a root of $ \text{scaleRoots}(p, \text{den}(x)) $.
